paper: Codina (2001), Pressure Stability in Fractional Step FEM for Incompressible Flows, JCP 170(1):112-140
verdict_summary: Core theoretical claims C1/C2 replicated on 20x20 Q1 cavity Re=100; stabilized-scheme claims C3/C5 not tested.

open_questions.q: Does the OSS (orthogonal sub-scale) pressure-gradient projection actually recover delta-t-independent pressure control across the same delta-t sweep {0.1*dt_crit, dt_crit, 56*dt_crit} on the same 20x20 Q1 cavity, thereby closing claim C3?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md flags C3 as NOT TESTED; our from-scratch code implements only the unstabilized fractional-step (paper eqs. 15-17, 23-25, 28-30). The paper's Section 5 defines OSS with an extra Gramm-matrix inversion for the pressure-gradient projection that we did not implement. Without it, we can neither confirm nor contradict the paper's central practical claim.
next_steps: Extend codina_replication.py with the OSS pressure-gradient projection Pi_h(grad p) using a consistent-mass solve.
Add the OSS residual term to the pressure Poisson equation (paper Section 5).
Re-run the same three delta-t points and check that P_std and P_roughness_d2 become insensitive to delta-t.
Compare stabilized contours qualitatively to paper Fig 3.

open_questions.q: Why does our unstabilized second-order (gamma=1, theta=1/2) scheme diverge to P_std ~ 10^53 at 0.1*dt_crit while Codina's Fig 2 shows bounded (but oscillatory) contours at essentially the same parameters?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md 'Deviations' section notes the divergence and hypothesizes (a) Q1/Q1 amplifying the paper's already-weak ell-infinity bound and (b) one-shot Picard convection linearization providing no damping. The paper's precise convection-linearization strategy and any implicit damping are not fully specified in the extracted algorithm, so the true source of the magnitude gap remains open.
next_steps: Try Picard-to-convergence per step (iterate convection until velocity residual < tol) instead of one iteration.
Try Newton linearization of the convective term.
Try a small artificial viscosity or SUPG stabilization on the momentum equation only, leaving the pressure-projection question intact.
Compare bounded-vs-divergent behavior across these variants; report whether ordering (2nd worse than 1st) is preserved.

open_questions.q: Does the O(delta_t) / O(delta_t^2) temporal convergence of claim C5 (paper Fig 7) actually manifest once OSS stabilization is added, using the paper's exact manufactured solution (paper eq. 60) on the same 20x20 Q1 mesh?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md reports that the unstabilized MMS run failed to converge in delta-t (errors grew as delta-t shrank), which is *consistent* with C1/C2 but does not test C5. C5 explicitly hinges on the stabilized scheme, per the paper's own note that the unstabilized second-order variant is unstable.
next_steps: After OQ1 is done, plug the paper eq. 60 manufactured solution into cavity_run.py's MMS harness.
Sweep delta_t in a decade range and fit log(err_u), log(err_p) vs log(delta_t).
Verify slopes ~1 for theta=1 and ~2 for theta=1/2 stabilized.
Cross-check that spatial error is subdominant at 20x20 (may need to run on a finer mesh to isolate temporal order).

open_questions.q: Is the pressure-stability ordering (second-order worse than first-order in unstabilized Q1/Q1) robust to (a) mesh refinement N in {10, 20, 40, 80} and (b) Reynolds number sweeps beyond Re=100?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md tests a single mesh (N=20) at a single Reynolds number (Re=100) at a single geometry (lid-driven cavity). The paper's underlying matrix argument in Section 3 is asymptotic and mesh/Re-independent, but the observed order-of-magnitude gap could in principle be sensitive to h and to convective dominance.
next_steps: Run the same delta-t triple on N in {10, 20, 40, 80} and check whether the first-order sqrt(delta_t) scaling holds cleanly.
Sweep Re in {1, 100, 400, 1000}; at higher Re, watch for convective instability confounding the pressure-stability signal.
Confirm that the second-order-worse-than-first-order ordering persists.
Report whether the log-log slope of P_std vs delta_t stays near 0.5 for first-order across N.

open_questions.q: Does the pressure-pin choice (node 0 fixed at p=0) or an alternative gauge fix (zero-mean pressure via Lagrange multiplier) affect the pressure-quality metrics P_std and P_roughness_d2, and could gauge choice partially explain the magnitude gap in OQ2?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md 'Genuine Critique' notes we pin p_0 = 0 to remove the singular Neumann mode, and Codina does not specify a gauge. P_std should be gauge-invariant (mean-subtracted), but the roughness proxy and the corrector-step scaling could interact with the pin location, especially when the pressure field is on the edge of blowing up.
next_steps: Swap the pin: try pinning a central node instead of node 0.
Try a zero-mean pressure constraint via a Lagrange multiplier row.
Re-run the same six cavity cases and check whether P_std, P_roughness_d2 are invariant (they should be) and whether the second-order divergence timing/magnitude shifts.
If magnitudes change, isolate the gauge effect from the intrinsic instability.
